jess (customer): hey team — BeaconCo is hitting lots of 429/short-circuit errors on our Dedicated pool (dedicated-pool-7a) since ~10:40 UTC. Started after a handful of very long-context requests. Latency spikes, some requests never finish, and customer billing looks off (huge token counts). can someone triage? @maria

maria (support): thanks jess. can you paste 1-2 request_ids + sample timestamps? any recent deploys to that pool?

jess (customer): request_id=01H8X2A9, request_id=01H8X2F1. No deploys in last 24h. Quick paste from their logs: 
```
WARN throttler: tenant=beaconco pool=dedicated-pool-7a reason=kv_cache_pressure evict_rate=95/s long_ctx_active=120 avg_kv_frag_pct=44
ERROR api: tenant=beaconco request=01H8X2A9 status=429 route=/v1/generate latency_ms=3120 notes="throttled:kv_eviction"
```

chad (infra): sketching this: looks like heavy KV churn + fragmentation. eviction_rate ~95/s is high for a single tenant on a small pool. two things to check: (1) kv.cache.evictions_total, kv.cache.fragmentation_bytes, kv.cache.prefetch_hit_ratio from metrics; (2) autoscaler events (cooldowns) — if pool is in cooldown it won't add replicas fast enough.

sara (eng-runtime): creating a minimal list: possible root causes are long-context requests blowing up KV working set, cache thrash due to many distinct prefixes, or jemalloc fragmentation making usable memory lower than physical. quick mitigations: enable prefix caching for that tenant, temporarily reduce tenant max_context_len, or scale the pool up manually. also check if prefix/KV compaction job has lagged.

maria (support): can you give repro steps we can hand BeaconCo? they can run a reduced test to show the behavior.

jess (customer): repro snippet they've been using (shortened):
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://dedicated.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"long-13b","input":"<repeat 50k tokens pattern>","stream":false}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```
It kicks off and sometimes succeeds, sometimes returns 429 after a few hundred tokens.

chad (infra): run this on the pool host to pull metrics quickly:
```
curl -sS http://metrics.internal.local/metrics?tenant=beaconco | grep -E "kv_cache|evictions|fragmentation"
```
sample output we received from the host: 
```
kv_cache_evictions_total{pool="dedicated-pool-7a",tenant="beaconco"} 12345
kv_cache_eviction_rate{pool="dedicated-pool-7a"} 95.2
kv_cache_fragmentation_bytes{host="gpu-17"} 48372928
kv_cache_prefix_hit_ratio{tenant="beaconco"} 0.12
```

sara (eng-runtime): that prefix_hit_ratio ~0.12 explains the thrash — most requests miss the prefix cache so KV working set grows. also the fragmentation_bytes ~48MB on that host if repeated across replicas means less contiguous allocs for KV pages. short-term: set tenant flag `prefix_cache=true` and `max_context_len=8192` for BeaconCo, and pin them to a slightly smaller model variant with better KV locality. I'll add the exact operator command.

sara (eng-runtime): operator command (run from infra ctl):
```
redwoodctl tenants update beaconco --set prefix_cache=true --set max_context_len=8192 --pool dedicated-pool-7a
```

maria (support): we'll propose that as a mitigation to the customer. any changes we should make on autoscaler side?

chad (infra): autoscaler events show recent scale-down 2m before spike -> then multiple bursty long-ctx requests. autoscaler has 300s cooldown so it didn't scale up quickly. deploy-bot just queued a scale event: "autoscaler: scale queued pool=dedicated-pool-7a delta=+2 (cooldown remaining 240s)". we can (a) force scale now to add +2 replicas or (b) bump desired_replicas for that pool for 30m. forcing scale is fastest.

blake (eng-runtime lead): I'm on it. sara, can you run a quick heap/jemalloc stats on the affected hosts and check KV compaction backlog? also open ENG ticket so we can track rollback if mitigation impacts throughput. I'll DM infra for manual scale.

sara (eng-runtime): copying commands:
```
ssh gpu-17 sudo /usr/local/bin/jemalloc-stats | egrep "unused|allocated|mapped"
kill -USR1 <runtime_pid>  # dumps KV compaction queue sizes into /var/log/redwood/kv_compact.log
```
sample compaction snippet: 
```
kv_compact.queue_len=0.12 avg_ms=45 tenants_compacted=3
```

maria (support): i'll give BeaconCo the mitigation plan: 1) short-term: apply tenant flags (prefix cache on + cap context to 8k), 2) we'll do manual scale +2 replicas, 3) eng-runtime will run jemalloc/compaction checks, 4) we'll monitor evictions and p99 latency for 1h before reverting.

jess (customer): thanks — please keep me posted, their SRE is on standby. one ask: if we throttle long contexts at the API layer, is that a supported pattern?

sara (eng-runtime): yes, per-tenant soft-limits are supported and safe. we prefer soft-limits + guidance because hard rejects change user behavior. set `max_context_len` and `long_request_qos=deprioritize` is a pattern we've used.

chad (infra): I'll manual scale now. follow-up: if eviction rate doesn't drop within 15m after scale + tenant flags, we'll repro in our lab with same long-ctx pattern and capture pprof + heap before/after.

blake (eng-runtime lead): opened ENG-3245 for tracking, assigned to @sara. maria, please add any customer screenshots to the ticket. i'll ping oncall if we need emergency rollback.

maria (support): noted. will update BeaconCo and paste logs to ENG-3245. 

chad (infra): manual scale applied at 10:53 UTC (scale +2). monitoring now.

sara (eng-runtime): got it. running jemalloc dump now and watching compaction logs. will post results in <10m.

jess (customer): appreciated everyone, will confirm once their traffic calms. :pray:
